info.title: Presend API
info.description: Presend's free API: 48 endpoints for security, verification, blockchain/crypto compliance, and everyday developer utilities. No signup, no API key, no paid tiers (per-minute rate limits apply). Covers file hashing & malware/phishing checks, JWT decode/verify, DNS & WHOIS lookup, package vulnerability and typosquatting checks, IP reputation, redirect-chain tracing, GitHub repo health signals, Cosmos SDK transaction decoding, OFAC sanctions screening for crypto addresses, CometBFT RPC auditing, IBAN/VAT validation, link metadata extraction, direct CVE lookup, PDF/image tools, and more.

post.description: Returns SHA-256, SHA-1 and SHA-512 for a file up to 20MB.

post.summary: Detect real file type from binary signature
post.description: Detects a file's real type from its binary signature ("magic bytes"), and flags a mismatch against the claimed Content-Type -- catches disguised files that slip past naive upload filters.

example.warning: Claimed type "image/jpeg" does not match the file's actual signature (detected: "image/png"). This can indicate a disguised or mislabeled file.

post.summary: Hash a file and check it against known malware
post.description: Computes SHA-256 and checks it against MalwareBazaar (abuse.ch), a free database of confirmed malware samples. Only catches already-known samples -- a 'not found' result does not guarantee the file is safe.

example.verdict: Not found in MalwareBazaar. This does not guarantee the file is safe — only that this exact file is not currently known to this database.

get.description: Validates an IBAN via the ISO 7064 mod-97 checksum, with country-specific length checks. No external data source -- pure algorithm.

parameters.name: iban
parameters.description: IBAN to validate. Spaces are ignored.

get.summary: Extract Open Graph / Twitter Card metadata from a URL
get.description: Extracts title, description, canonical URL, Open Graph tags, Twitter Card tags and the favicon from a page's <head> -- the same data used to render a link preview card in a chat app. Redirects are followed, each hop validated against private and internal addresses; final_url is where they ended, and relative URLs in the page (og:image, for instance) resolve against it. favicon_source is "declared" when the page declares an icon, "default" when /favicon.ico is only a guess (not checked).

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: URL to extract metadata from.

get.description: Decodes the header and payload of a JWT. Does not verify the signature.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The JWT to decode. Decodes header and payload only -- does not verify the signature (use /jwt-verify for that).

post.description: Actually verifies the signature (HS256/384/512, RS/PS256/384/512, ES256/384/512) via the Workers-native Web Crypto API, plus exp/nbf claim checks. Unlike /jwt-decode, this performs real cryptographic verification.

token.description: The JWT to verify. Checks the cryptographic signature -- use /jwt-decode if you only need to read the header and payload.

jwk.description: Public key in JWK format, for RS/PS/ES algorithms.

jwks_url.description: URL to a JWKS document; the key is matched by the token's "kid" header.

get.description: Returns the caller's IP with city, country, currency, language, EU flag, and Tor exit-node detection (official Tor Project public list). Geolocation is read directly from Cloudflare's edge — no third-party API call.
Current time, or convert between Unix timestamp and ISO date.

get.summary: Check if a password has been breached
get.description: Uses HIBP k-anonymity — only 5 hash chars are sent externally.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Password to check against known data-breach corpora. Only a 5-character SHA-1 hash prefix is sent to HIBP (k-anonymity), but the password itself travels in this request's URL; for real passwords, prefer the password-check endpoint (POST body).

post.description: Chains entropy/strength scoring with an optional HIBP breach check in a single call. Password is sent in the JSON body, never in a URL. Entropy is an upper bound (random choice assumed; a passphrase is estimated per word); a password found in breaches is always rated very_weak.

password.description: Password to evaluate for strength (length, character variety, common patterns).

check_breach.description: Whether to also check the password against known data-breach corpora via k-anonymity. true or false.

200.description: Strength analysis and optional breach result

estimate_basis.description: What the entropy estimate assumes: random characters, or random words for a passphrase (3+ words of letters).

strength_reason.description: found_in_breaches: the password appears in Have I Been Pwned data, so strength is very_weak and crack time instant whatever the entropy.

example.entropy_note: Upper bound: assumes the characters (or, for a passphrase, the words) were chosen at random. Dictionary words, names, dates and keyboard patterns are far weaker than this estimate.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Email address to check against a list of known disposable/temporary email domains.

get.description: Chains syntax check, MX lookup, disposable-domain detection, and generic/role-account detection in a single call.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Email address to run through combined syntax, disposable-domain, and MX-record checks.

valid.description: true: syntax OK, MX record found, not disposable. false: conclusive failure, see reason. null: the MX lookup could not be completed (reason mx_lookup_failed); retry later, do not treat as invalid.

reason.description: invalid_syntax, no_mx_record, disposable_domain or mx_lookup_failed; null when valid is true.

get.summary: Validate and format a phone number
get.description: Validates and formats via libphonenumber-js. If “country” is omitted for a number without a leading +, the caller's IP-derived country (Cloudflare edge geolocation) is used as the default.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: Phone number to validate and format, ideally in E.164 format (e.g. +14155552671).

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g. US, FR), used to interpret a number with no leading +.

get.description: Checks SPF strength, DMARC policy, and a best-effort DKIM lookup against common selectors. DKIM has no fixed DNS location, so absence of a match does not prove DKIM is unconfigured.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Domain to check SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records for, e.g. example.com.

dkim.note: Best-effort: only common selectors are tested. A domain can have valid DKIM under a custom selector not listed here — absence of a match does not prove DKIM is unconfigured.

get.description: Combines security-headers, url-reputation, and subdomains into a single overall score and verdict, run in parallel.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: URL to run a combined security posture check against (headers, reputation, and related signals).

get.summary: Check which AI crawlers are allowed by robots.txt
get.description: Fetches robots.txt and reports which known AI crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, CCBot, etc.) are allowed or blocked. Free, no signup required.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Domain to check, e.g. example.com. robots.txt is fetched from https://<domain>/robots.txt.

example.wildcard_rules_note: Shown once here; any bot below with matched_by="wildcard" is governed by these rules (no bot-specific override).

post.description: Merges 2+ PDF files into one document, then compresses the result and strips metadata (title, author, producer). Chains two operations in a single call — most free APIs require calling merge and compress separately and gluing the results together yourself.

files.description: 2 or more PDF files, max 20 files / 30MB total.

post.description: Removes EXIF/GPS data from JPEG (APP1 segment) and text metadata from PNG (tEXt/zTXt/iTXt/eXIf/tIME chunks) via direct binary parsing. Pixel data is never re-encoded, so there is zero quality loss — unlike canvas-based approaches, which always recompress.

200.description: Cleaned image, same format as input

post.description: Computes a perceptual hash (dHash, 64-bit) for 1 or 2 JPEG/PNG images. Unlike a cryptographic hash, this survives re-compression, minor resizing, and small edits. Send 2 images to get a direct similarity comparison.

files.description: 1 file (hash only) or 2 files (compare). JPEG/PNG, max 10MB each.

200.description: Hash (1 file) or comparison result (2 files)

example.verdict: Near-identical (likely the same image, possibly re-compressed or lightly edited).

post.summary: Text similarity via SimHash (1 or 2 texts)
post.description: Computes a 64-bit SimHash (over word shingles) for 1 or 2 texts. Unlike a cryptographic hash, this detects paraphrased or lightly-edited near-duplicate content. Send 2 texts to get a direct similarity comparison. Unrelated texts typically score ~50% by chance, not 0%.

texts.description: 1 text (hash only) or 2 texts (compare). Max 200,000 characters each.

200.description: Hash (1 text) or comparison result (2 texts)

example.verdict: Near-identical (likely the same text, possibly with trivial edits).

get.description: Checks a package/version against OSV.dev (Google's Open Source Vulnerabilities database) -- npm, PyPI, Go, crates.io, Maven, RubyGems, Packagist, NuGet.

parameters.name: ecosystem
parameters.description: Package ecosystem, e.g. npm, PyPI, Go, crates.io, Maven, RubyGems, Packagist, or NuGet.

parameters.name: package
parameters.description: Package name to check against OSV.dev for known CVEs.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: Omit to check all versions of the package.

scope.description: Which versions the result covers: "version <x>", or "all versions" when no version is given (advisories affecting any version, including old ones, are counted).

existence.description: Whether the package exists on its registry. Checked for npm and PyPI when OSV.dev returns no advisory: not_found = no package with this name; unavailable = the registry could not be reached; not_checked = other ecosystems.

found.description: Present, and false, when no package with this name exists on npm or PyPI.

note.description: Explains a not-found package, an unconfirmed existence, a missing version or truncated results.

results_truncated.description: true when OSV.dev returned more than 5 pages of results; only the first 5 are counted.

vulnerable.description: true if at least one advisory matches. null when the package does not exist on npm or PyPI, or when its existence could not be confirmed: never read null as clean.

vulnerabilities.summary: Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) in lodash
lodash vulnerable to Prototype Pollution via array path bypass in `_.unset` and `_.omit`
lodash vulnerable to Code Injection via `_.template` imports key names
Lodash has Prototype Pollution Vulnerability in `_.unset` and `_.omit` functions

example.source: OSV.dev (Google) -- aggregates the GitHub Advisory Database plus ecosystem-native advisories.

post.description: Checks up to 100 package names in one request, counted as a single request for rate limiting. Same analysis as GET; an invalid entry yields {package, error} instead of failing the batch.

results.description: One entry per input name, in input order. Same fields as the GET response, or {package, error} for an invalid entry.

400.description: Invalid JSON body, unsupported ecosystem, empty list, or more than 100 names

get.description: Flags package names that are a near-miss of a curated list of well-known npm/PyPI packages (Damerau-Levenshtein: 1 edit for 4-7 character names, 2 for 8+; names of 3 characters or fewer are not fuzzy-matched) -- the classic typosquatting pattern. A batch POST variant is available.

parameters.name: ecosystem
parameters.description: Package ecosystem, e.g. npm or PyPI.

parameters.name: package
parameters.description: Package name to check for likely typosquatting of a well-known package in the given ecosystem.

200.description: Typosquatting analysis for the package name

known_legitimate.description: True when the name resembles a well-known package but is itself a manually reviewed legitimate package (e.g. preact vs react, psycopg vs psycopg2). Such names are not flagged as suspicious.

example.note: Name is within edit-distance 2 of a well-known package. Verify this is the package you meant to install, not a look-alike.
example.source: Curated list of ~165 well-known npm packages, checked via Damerau-Levenshtein edit distance (transpositions, omissions, insertions, substitutions). Not an exhaustive top-N-by-downloads feed.

get.summary: IP reputation check against a curated blocklist
get.description: Checks an IPv4 or IPv6 address against a curated list of netblocks known to be hijacked or controlled by spam/cyber-crime operations. The list copy is refreshed at most once a day; the response includes the list date, attribution and a stale flag if the upstream source has been unreachable long enough for the copy to be over 48 hours old. Free, no signup.

parameters.name: ip
parameters.description: IPv4 or IPv6 address to check (IPv4-mapped IPv6 such as ::ffff:1.2.3.4 is checked against the IPv4 list) against a curated list of known hijacked or cyber-crime-controlled netblocks.

list_date.description: Date of the list version used (YYYY-MM-DD)

stale.description: True if the list copy is older than 48 hours (upstream unreachable)

example.source: Spamhaus DROP (Don't Route Or Peer) -- netblocks known to be hijacked or controlled by spam/cyber-crime operations. IPv4 and IPv6 (separate lists). Spamhaus re-evaluates listings daily; this service refreshes its copy at most once a day.

get.description: Checks a crypto address against every OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) digital currency address list (per-asset lists such as ETH, USDT, USDC, XBT, TRX). EVM (0x...) and Bitcoin (bc1..., 1..., 3...) addresses are fully covered: sanctioned is true or false, with the matching lists. Addresses of other chains are flagged when listed. Cosmos SDK (bech32) addresses return sanctioned: null when not listed, since OFAC has published no entries for Cosmos SDK chains. Free, no signup.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: Address to screen: EVM (0x + 40 hex chars) or Bitcoin (bc1..., 1..., 3...), both fully covered. Addresses of other chains are matched against their lists too; bech32 addresses of other chains (e.g. cosmos1...) return sanctioned: null (unchecked, not clean) when not listed.

example.source: OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, digital currency addresses (all per-asset lists), republished nightly by 0xB10C/ofac-sanctioned-digital-currency-addresses from the official sdn_advanced.xml.
example.note: Not on any OFAC SDN digital currency address list. This is one specific, US-government sanctions list -- not a full risk score, and a clean result here does not mean the address is otherwise trustworthy.

get.description: Decodes a raw, signed Cosmos SDK transaction (protobuf TxRaw bytes, base64-encoded) into readable JSON -- messages, fee, gas, signer info, and signatures. Hand-rolled protobuf reader, no external dependency. Message contents are decoded for common bank/staking/gov/authz types (including recursive MsgExec, up to a depth cap); other types are returned as their type URL plus raw hex. Free, no signup.

parameters.name: tx
parameters.description: Base64-encoded Cosmos SDK TxRaw protobuf bytes, as returned by any chain's CometBFT RPC /block (result.block.data.txs[]) or /tx_search endpoints.

get.summary: CometBFT RPC health and safety audit
get.description: Audits a public CometBFT RPC endpoint for a Cosmos SDK chain: node status, health, peer connectivity, and whether unsafe administrative RPC methods (dial_seeds, dial_peers, unsafe_flush_mempool) appear to be publicly exposed. Read-only -- never invokes any unsafe method itself; exposure is detected by inspecting the node's own passive route listing. Free, no signup.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Base URL of a CometBFT RPC endpoint to audit.

post.description: Checks up to 20 packages (npm, or pypi for existence and age only) in one request, counted as a single request for rate limiting. Same analysis as GET; a missing package yields found=false and a registry failure or invalid entry yields an error field, without failing the batch.

results.description: One entry per input name, in input order. Same fields as the GET response, or {package, error} for an invalid entry.

400.description: Invalid JSON body, unsupported ecosystem, empty list, or more than 20 names

get.summary: Detect a suspicious npm package maintainer change
get.description: Flags a previously unseen human publisher taking over an npm package after 180+ days of inactivity, within the last 365 days -- the pattern behind the event-stream compromise (2018). Older handoffs are counted but not flagged; transitions to npm trusted publishing (verified OIDC identity, not just a bot-like account name) and pre-release versions are reported separately without raising the flag. Does NOT detect a hijacked existing maintainer account (ua-parser-js, 2021) or a malicious release by an existing maintainer (colors.js, 2022). A batch POST variant is available. npm only for now. For PyPI (ecosystem=pypi), only existence and age are reported: found, first_published, package_age_days, new_package (oldest file still on PyPI, age_basis oldest_file_on_pypi), with maintainer_analysis npm_only and suspicious null, because PyPI does not expose who published each release.

parameters.name: ecosystem
parameters.description: npm (full analysis) or pypi (existence and age only; no publisher-change analysis).

parameters.name: package
parameters.description: Package name, e.g. lodash

200.description: Maintainer change analysis for the package

first_published.description: Creation date recorded by the npm registry (time.created), read from the registry document already fetched. Absent when found is false.

new_package.description: true when the package was first published less than 30 days ago (a squatted or invented name is usually recent). Does not change suspicious.

maintainer_analysis.description: npm_only on PyPI results: the publisher-change analysis is not available for PyPI. Absent for npm.

age_basis.description: oldest_file_on_pypi on PyPI results (deleted releases make a project look younger). Absent for npm, where first_published is the registry's creation date.

publisher_check.description: Whether the new publisher's other packages could be looked up. unavailable (e.g. npm search rate limit): the event stays flagged without that check.

trusted_publisher.description: Trusted publishing provider id set by the npm registry (e.g. github, gitlab). Only verified trusted publishing exempts an event; a bot-like account name does not.

established_publisher_events.description: Events whose new publisher already maintains another widely used npm package (100,000+ weekly downloads, excluding this one): most likely a legitimate maintainer handover. Reported, but they do not trigger suspicious.

example.note: Flags a previously unseen human publisher taking over after 180+ days of inactivity, within the last 365 days. New publishers who already maintain another widely used package (100,000+ weekly downloads) are listed under established_publisher_events without triggering suspicious. Heuristic signal for manual review, not proof of compromise. Does not detect a hijacked existing account or a malicious release by an existing maintainer.

get.description: Combines maintainer-change-check (npm only), vulnerability-check, typosquat-check, and repo-health-check (auto-resolved from registry metadata when possible) into a single call with one overall verdict. overall_risk is review_recommended when any check raises a flag; if a check could not run (rate limit, upstream error), it is listed in unavailable_checks and the verdict is incomplete, never no_signals_found. A package that does not exist on npm or PyPI gets package_not_found (registry_status not_found, with registry_note), never no_signals_found: the name may be invented, for instance by an AI model. Vulnerabilities are checked for the given version, or the latest published one. A package first published less than 30 days ago gets the new_package flag (overall_risk review_recommended): first_published and package_age_days give its age, and age_basis says how it was measured (npm: the registry's creation date; PyPI: the oldest file still on PyPI, so a project that deleted its earlier releases looks new). Being new does not make a package malicious; it means the name is worth checking before installing.

parameters.name: ecosystem
parameters.description: Package ecosystem. maintainer-change-check only runs for npm.

parameters.name: package
parameters.description: Package name to check.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: Exact version to check for known vulnerabilities. Optional: defaults to the latest published version (npm and PyPI); the version actually checked is returned in version_checked.

registry_status.description: npm and PyPI only: found, not_found (the registry has no such package) or unavailable (registry error, the verdict is then incomplete).

first_published.description: npm: creation date recorded by the registry. PyPI: upload date of the oldest file still on PyPI (earlier releases may have been deleted). Null if the package was not found or no date is available.

new_package.description: true when package_age_days is below new_package_threshold_days; the new_package flag is then added. Null when the age is unknown.

new_package_threshold_days.description: Age below which a package is reported as new (30).

age_basis.description: registry_created_date (npm) or oldest_file_on_pypi (PyPI); null when no age is available.

unavailable_checks.description: Checks that could not run (rate limit, upstream error).

version_note.description: Set when no version could be determined: vulnerability results then cover all versions.
